newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares lose 1.5 pct on high o/n rates.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares lose 1.5 pct on high o/n rates.

text.p: Istanbul shares retreated in quiet trade on Wednesday amid high overnight money and repo rates caused by a severe cash shortage in the money market, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 2,005, down 31 points, or 1.52 percent from Tuesday after moving between 1,997 and 2,040.
Trade volume inched up to 15.4 trillion lira ($94 million) on Wednesday, from Tuesday's 15.2 trillion ($93 million).

"Lack of liquidity is the main reason behind the fall which is also the cause of high money and repo rates. Under these conditions, I expect the index to break 2,000 support and fall further towards new technical support seen at 1,970," said Murat Ozkan from Emper Securities.

Turkish central bank heavily funded banks via open market and interbank due to a severe liquidity shortage. Nevertheless, the average overnight repo rate jumped to 79.84 percent from Tuesday's 72.31 percent and the average overnight money rate firmed to 73.85 percent from previous 73.75.

"I think foreigners will enter the market at below the 2,000 level because they are optimistic about Turkish shares. I see today's fall as temporary because of the new government's tight monetary policy," said Cenk Durust, in charge of foreign customers division in ABN AMRO's Istanbul branch said.
